name: Cabeza de Vaca across the continent
traveler: Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca, Estevanico, Dorantes and Castillo
summary: Of the 300 men of the Narváez expedition stranded in Florida, four survive eight years as castaways, traders and healers among the peoples of the Gulf coast and the Southwest, and walk to Mexico. Their stories of rich cities to the north send Coronado out to look for them.

stops.note: Narváez lands 300 men and sends the ships away.
Starving, they build rafts of horsehide and sail west along the coast.
The rafts are wrecked; the Karankawa take in the survivors.
After six years as slaves and traders, four men escape inland.
Famous as healers, they are passed from village to village.
Villagers tell of great towns to the north and give them turquoise and emeralds.
They meet Spanish slavers, to the soldiers' astonishment.
Received by the viceroy; their report sets off the search for Cíbola.

informs.note: Rumours of rich towns to the north
